description: Research competitors' public Google, Facebook and Instagram ads in ChatGPT from the Google Ads Transparency Center and Meta Ad Library. Read-only.

capabilities: Find a competitor's Google advertiser or Facebook Page by brand, company or Page name
List the Google ads associated with a competitor website or advertiser, by country and date range
List a competitor's Facebook and Instagram ads with text, headline, call to action, links and media
Read Google ad headlines, descriptions, images and videos for selected creatives
Read the payer, selected audience and reach Meta publishes for ads delivered in the EU and UK
No ad account needed; read-only public data with no budgets, spend or performance
defaultPrompt: Use $getting-started-adlibrary to show the Google and Meta ads my main competitor is running right now.
Show me the Google ads that run for allbirds.com in the United States over the last 30 days.
What ads is Gymshark running on Facebook and Instagram in the UK right now?
interface.longDescription:
Research competitors' ads in ChatGPT with LoomaScale, using the public Google Ads Transparency Center and Meta Ad Library (formerly the Facebook Ad Library). Built for advertisers, small businesses and agencies who want to see what competitors run before planning their own ads.

What ads is my competitor running on Google?
Find the ads associated with a competitor website, or with a public advertiser you look up by name, in a country and date range. Each creative comes with its format, first and last shown dates and a Transparency Center link. Read a few creatives for their headlines, descriptions, images, videos and the URL shown in the ad.

What ads is my competitor running on Facebook and Instagram?
Find the competitor's Facebook Page in the Meta Ad Library, then list the ads it runs in one country, with text, headline, call to action, links, carousel cards, images, videos, delivery dates and the Meta apps each ad runs on. Search ad text by keyword across all advertisers, too.

Who paid for an ad, and how many people did it reach?
For ads delivered in the EU or the UK, read the payer and beneficiary, the locations, ages and gender the advertiser selected, and the number of accounts reached by country, age and gender.

What can it not show?
Public ad libraries do not reveal budgets, spend, bids, targeting interests, conversions or which ad performs best. An empty result does not prove a competitor is not advertising.

Do I need an ad account?
No. Sign in to LoomaScale and allow access; nothing is connected. Helper tools check your usage, list the data sources you can connect, or send a feature request when you ask.

LoomaScale is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google or Meta.

name: loomascale-adlibrary

positive.description: Find a competitor's Google ads by website.
positive.prompt: Show me the Google ads that run for allbirds.com in the United States over the last 30 days, and read the text of the three most recent ones.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Google Ads Transparency Center creatives for allbirds.com in the United States with advertiser, format and first/last shown dates, then reads the headlines and descriptions of three of them. Nothing is changed in any account.

positive.description: Find a competitor's Google advertiser by name.
positive.prompt: Find Gymshark in the Google Ads Transparency Center and list the Google ads they ran in the United Kingdom over the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the matching Google advertisers with their verification status and ad count range, picks (or asks the user to pick) the Gymshark advertiser, then lists its UK creatives with format and first/last shown dates.

positive.description: Find a competitor's Meta ads by brand.
positive.prompt: What ads is Gymshark running on Facebook and Instagram in the UK right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Gymshark Facebook Page in the Meta Ad Library, then lists its active UK ads with text, headline, call to action, format and delivery dates.

positive.description: Read EU reach disclosures for one Meta ad.
positive.prompt: Find the ads Gymshark is running on Facebook in Germany, then for the first one tell me who paid for it and how many people in the EU it reached.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Gymshark's active ads in Germany, then returns the first ad's payer and beneficiary, selected locations, ages and gender, and accounts reached by country, age and gender as Meta publishes them for EU delivery.

positive.description: Search Meta ads by keyword across advertisers.
positive.prompt: Show me Facebook and Instagram ads active in the United States that mention "meal kit", and summarize the offers they use.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists active US ads from any advertiser whose text matches "meal kit", with Page, text, headline and call to action, then summarizes the offers. No advertiser needs to be named first.

negative.description: Changing the user's own campaigns is outside this integration.
negative.prompt: Pause my Google Ads campaign called Brand Search.
negative.expected_behavior: The app should not be invoked to change campaigns; this Ad Library integration only reads public competitor ads and cannot pause, edit or create anything.

negative.description: Competitor spend and performance are not public.
negative.prompt: How much does Nike spend on Facebook ads per month and which ad gets the most conversions?
negative.expected_behavior: The app should not claim spend or conversion figures; public ad libraries show ads, dates and (for the EU/UK) reach, never budgets, spend or conversions.

negative.description: Organic SEO rankings are outside this integration.
negative.prompt: What position does my website rank for "best running shoes" on Google?
negative.expected_behavior: The app should not be invoked; the Ad Library integration researches public ads, not organic search rankings.
